citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The facility failed to sanitize the primary enclosure for two domestic cats. The primary enclosure for two Bengal cats is
covered in foliage, and the wooden beams and wire mesh is covered in algae. The licensee remarked he did not know he
was supposed to sanitize the enclosure.
Sanitizing is important to prevent the accumulation and transmission of harmful bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites that
threaten feline health. It reduces zoonotic risks associated with pathogens such as Toxoplasma gondii and Salmonella.
Compliance requires daily spot cleaning and full sanitization every two weeks, and it’s recommended to maintain
documentation verifying adherence to these standards.
Used primary enclosures and food and water receptacles for dogs and cats must be sanitized at least once every 2 weeks
using one of the methods prescribed in paragraph (b)(3) of this section, and more often if necessary to prevent an
accumulation of dirt, debris, food waste, excreta, and other disease hazards. Correct by September 17, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
